name: Ilya Volodarsky
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the Y Combinator company page for Segment names him -- 'Founded in 2011 by Ilya Volodarsky, Segment has 550 employees based in San Francisco' (https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/segment). SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: no earlier venture found. CNBC's founding account is explicit that the three MIT roommates 'didn't start out dreaming of being entrepreneurs' and only formed a company after a 2010 class; his pre-Segment roles named in secondary bios (Microsoft, LeanServer, MIT Media Lab) are employment/research, not ventures, and Segment.io Inc is the same legal entity through the ClassMetric lecture-tool and web-analytics pivots, so the 2011 founding is both a4 and the hit entity's birth. IPO/ACQ FALLBACK BARRED: Segment never IPO'd, and the Twilio acquisition (Nov 2020) is known to postdate the crossing by years, so acq50 would be years late; a bounded rev10 is recorded instead per frame.md. BOUNDED rev10 2011-2019, both ends sourced. Lower end: the company was founded in 2011 and cannot have earned before it existed; CNBC records the first product launched in autumn 2011, failed, and the investors were refunded, so 2011 revenue is nil. Upper end: Twilio's FY2020 10-K discloses unaudited pro forma combined revenue of $1,217,502k for the year ended 31 Dec 2019 (Segment treated as if acquired 1 Jan 2019) against Twilio's own audited 2019 revenue of $1,134,468k in the same filing, implying Segment standalone 2019 revenue of about $83.0m -- roughly 10x the 2019 constant-dollar rev10 bar of $7,941,064. Corroborated directly in the same filing: Segment contributed $23.0m of revenue in the stub period 2 Nov - 31 Dec 2020 alone, itself ~2.9x the 2020 bar of $8,039,032. The span is 8 years, inside the 10-year limit; midpoint 2015. The bracket was not narrowed further because the only year-by-year figures found for 2013 ($1m) and 2017 ($36m) come from getlatka.com, an estimate aggregator, and were judged too weak to carry a bound. a1: unknown after two attempts -- his Forbes profile page carries no age or birth year and no other source publishes one. a2 JUDGMENT CALL (low): he is a dropout, so the anchor is the last COMPLETED credential, which is his high-school diploma; no source names his school or graduation year, but two sources independently place his MIT matriculation in 2008 (yourtechstory.com: the co-founders 'met Ilya Volodarsky in 2008, during the campus preview weekend at MIT', an event for admitted freshmen held each April; theorg.com's LinkedIn-derived entry gives MIT 2008-2012), and Forbes titles its piece on the three of them 'Success Without A Diploma: How 3 MIT Dropouts Made It Big'. CNBC adds that they took a leave of absence in 2011 'with a year left at MIT'. Recorded 2008 at low confidence on that basis; the alternative reading is a2=unknown, as used for p114. a3 UNKNOWN: secondary bios list Microsoft, LeanServer and the MIT Media Lab before Segment, but no source dates any of them, so per the brief this is unknown rather than set equal to a4. a6: 2020, Twilio's agreement to acquire Segment for approximately $3.2bn, announced 12 Oct 2020 and closed 2 Nov 2020 (Twilio 8-K exhibit 99.1).

name: Jeff Bezos
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/jeff-bezos/ names him, 'Chairman and Founder, Amazon', '$266.6B', '#3 in the world today' (fetched 22 Aug 2026); Forbes scores him self-made. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: no earlier venture found. Wikipedia's account records no business he started before Amazon; his pre-1994 work was all salaried (Fitel 1986-88, Bankers Trust 1988-90, D. E. Shaw 1990-94). The teenage 'Dream Institute' summer camp is not documented in the sources consulted and in any case had no revenue near the bar. PINNED rev10 1996, not bounded and not the IPO. Amazon's own S-1 (filed 24 Mar 1997) gives audited net sales of $--, $511k and $15,746k for 1994, 1995 and 1996; the 1995 figure of $0.511m is far below that year's constant-dollar bar of $4,733,757 and the 1996 figure of $15.746m is 3.23x the 1996 bar of $4,873,534, so the crossing falls inside calendar 1996 and needs no bracket. Margin at the crossing year is +223% over the bar -- well clear. IPO/ACQ FALLBACK NOT USED and correctly barred: the May 1997 IPO postdates the documented revenue crossing by a year, exactly the error frame.md warns about. The S-1's quarterly table shows the 1996 crossing happening within the year (Q1 $875k, Q2 $2,230k, Q3 $4,173k, Q4 $8,468k), which is corroboration, not a second anchor. a1: born 12 January 1964, Albuquerque NM. a2: 1986, BSE in electrical engineering and computer science, Princeton, summa cum laude -- highest credential, completed. a3 JUDGMENT CALL (low), rule R1 from docs/PILOT-REVIEW.md: the hit's field is online consumer retail and no employer-paid work in it precedes the venture, so a3 is set equal to a4 at 1994. His three prior employers were financial-services technology, not online retail; the competing reading is that Fitel (1986), where he built a network for cross-border trade, was his first software-domain job, which would move a3 eight years earlier. 1994 is also the year he ran D. E. Shaw's internet-business investigation, so the two internet-domain readings coincide on the year in any case. a4: Amazon founded 5 July 1994, Bellevue WA. a6: 1997 -- net sales of $147,758k in FY1997 per the FY1997 10-K, about 30x that year's bar, the year of the 15 May 1997 IPO.

name: Neal O'Mara
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the Y Combinator company page for HelloSign names him -- 'Founded in by Neal O'Mara, HelloSign has 100 employees based in San Francisco', batch Winter 2011 (https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/hellosign); the roster's quoted text, missing year and all, matches the live page. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: no earlier venture found. HelloFax is often described as a separate earlier company, but it is not: Dropbox's FY2019 10-K names the acquired entity 'JN Projects, Inc. (d/b/a HelloSign)' and refers to 'HelloSign's 2011 Equity Incentive Plan', so HelloFax (2011) and HelloSign (2012) are two products of one company incorporated in 2011, and the entity's founding is the venture date. His pre-HelloFax roles named in secondary profiles (TripIt, GE Healthcare) are salaried employment, not ventures. IPO/ACQ FALLBACK BARRED: HelloSign never IPO'd and the Dropbox acquisition (announced 28 Jan 2019, closed 8 Feb 2019, $230m cash) would date the row at or after the crossing, not at it; Dropbox's own CFO evidence below shows revenue above the bar in 2019 and the company was already at 112 employees in 2018, so a crossing before the acquisition is known and acq50 is not permitted. BOUNDED rev10 2011-2019, both ends sourced. Lower end: the company was founded and went through YC in 2011 with no revenue (YC batch W11; diginomica, 28 Jan 2019, 'Founded in 2011, HelloSign...'; CNBC says 2010, which would only widen the bracket and cannot contain a crossing because the company launched with nil revenue). Upper end: on Dropbox's Q1 2019 earnings call (9 May 2019) CFO Ajay Vashee said 'We continue to expect HelloSign to contribute just over a point of revenue growth this year' -- a point of growth on Dropbox's FY2018 revenue of $1,391.7m is about $13.9m, and that is stated as being NET of the purchase-accounting writedown of HelloSign's deferred revenue and net of a partial year of recognition, so standalone 2019 revenue was comfortably above $14m against a 2019 constant-dollar bar of $7,941,064, a margin of at least +75%. Span is 8 years, inside the 10-year limit; midpoint 2015. NARROWER READING CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: getlatka.com reports, from a dated interview with CEO Joseph Walla on 21 Nov 2016, that HelloSign 'Hit $7.2m revenue in November 2016' and $0 at launch in 2011, which would give a much tighter 2016-2019 bracket -- but $7.2m is only 3.4% BELOW the 2016 bar of $7,454,953, the figure is an ARR snapshot rather than a calendar-year revenue, and getlatka is an interview aggregator; a bound whose lower end turns on a 3.4% margin from a single secondary source is exactly the stretch the brief warns against, so the conservative founding-year bracket is recorded instead and the tighter reading is left here for the record. a1 UNKNOWN: no birth year published for him after two attempts. a2 UNKNOWN after two attempts: wellfound.com/p/neal-omara gives Bucknell University with no degree, no field and no years, and no other source dates his graduation; recorded unknown rather than guessed. a3 UNKNOWN: secondary profiles list TripIt and GE Healthcare before HelloFax, but no source dates either, so per the brief this is unknown rather than set equal to a4. a6: 2019, the $230m Dropbox acquisition (Dropbox FY2019 10-K Note 5, total purchase consideration $177.9m plus $48.5m tied to continuing service).

name: Mark Zuckerberg
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED via the roster's cited Forbes profile URL (https://www.forbes.com/profile/mark-zuckerberg/), Forbes World's Billionaires, self-made. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: no earlier venture found. ZuckNet (c.1995), Synapse Media Player (high school) and the Harvard-era CourseMatch and Facemash all predate Facebook, but none was a company and none is reported to have earned any revenue -- Wikipedia records that he declined offers for Synapse and released it free -- so none can have crossed the bar before 2004. Thefacebook (4 Feb 2004) is the first venture and the hit entity. PINNED rev10 2005. TechCrunch, writing on the day Facebook's S-1 was filed, states: 'Facebook made a modest $382,000 in revenue 2004, $9 million in revenue in 2005, $48 million in revenue in 2006' and '$153 million in revenue in 2007'. The 2004 figure of $0.382m is 6% of that year's constant-dollar rev10 bar of $5,867,498; the 2005 figure of $9m is 1.48x the 2005 bar of $6,066,291, so the crossing falls inside calendar 2005. MARGIN NOTE: +48% over the bar, the narrowest figure on this batch and single-sourced -- the S-1 itself only discloses 2007 onward, and two further attempts (Britannica Money, prioridata.com, lovemoney.com, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Facebook) produced no independent 2005 figure. If the $9m were wrong the crossing would move to 2006 ($48m vs a $6,261,978 bar), so the honest alternative reading is a bounded 2005-2006; 2005 is pinned because the same sentence supplies both the sub-bar 2004 figure and the above-bar 2005 figure and is a contemporaneous trade-press report at the S-1 moment. IPO/ACQ FALLBACK BARRED: revenue above the bar is documented from 2005, seven years before the May 2012 IPO. a1: born 14 May 1984. a2: 2002, graduated Phillips Exeter Academy -- a dropout, so the anchor is the last credential actually COMPLETED; he entered Harvard in 2002 and left in his second year with no degree, and the 25 May 2017 Harvard degree is honorary and not a completed credential. a3 JUDGMENT CALL (low), rule R1 from docs/PILOT-REVIEW.md: he had no employer-paid work of any kind before founding Facebook, so a3 is set equal to a4 at 2004. a4: 4 February 2004. a6: 2012 -- the 18 May 2012 IPO and the first FY 10-K (filed 1 Feb 2013), the year Facebook also passed one billion monthly users.

name: Gautam Adani
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/gautam-adani/ names him with '$92B', 'Commodities, infrastructure, Self Made', and 'Adani grew his company, which began in 1988 as a commodities trading firm, into new sectors' -- matching the roster's quoted text. rev10 USED, rank1 NOT USED: frame.md orders this bucket rev10 first and rank1 only where revenue is unavailable. A rank1 on Mundra Port cargo-throughput tables would date the row in the 2010s, two decades after the trading house crossed the bar, which is the same late-dating error the IPO fallback causes; it is therefore not used even though the bucket permits it. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK, the main risk on this row. Three pre-1988 activities were examined. (1) 1978, diamond sorter for Mahendra Brothers in Mumbai -- salaried employment, recorded as a3, not a venture. (2) 1981, 'his elder brother Mahasukhbhai Adani bought a plastics unit in Ahmedabad and invited him to manage the operations' -- an existing business he was invited to run, so assigned leadership rather than founding, the same treatment this dataset gives p18 Morris Chang's ITRI presidency and p22 Thomas Struengmann's Durachemie role. (3) 1985, 'he started importing primary polymers for small-scale industries' -- the one genuine ambiguity. Wikipedia frames it as an extension of the brother's plastics unit ('This venture turned out to be Adani's gateway to global trading through polyvinyl chloride imports'), gives it no firm name, and no source anywhere publishes a revenue figure for it; Forbes and Adani's own corporate timeline both date the company to 1988. It is therefore not recorded as a separate venture and not treated as the hit entity. JUDGMENT CALL: a4 is recorded as 1988 at medium confidence for that reason; the competing reading is a4=1985. Note that the two readings do not move a5, because frame.md brackets from the founding of the HIT ENTITY, which is Adani Exports (1988) on every source. BOUNDED rev10 1988-1998, both ends sourced, span exactly 10 years -- at the frame's maximum, which is why confidence is low. Lower end: Adani Exports was founded in 1988 as a partnership firm with a capital of Rs 5 lakh (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adani_Group; Forbes; adani.com timeline, 'Mr. Gautam Adani established Adani Exports that deals in agricultural commodities and power in Ahmedabad, Gujarat'), roughly $35-40k at the era's ~13 INR/USD -- about 1% of the 1988 constant-dollar rev10 bar of $3,674,564 -- and a company cannot earn before it exists. Upper end: Adani's corporate timeline states for 1998 'In 10 years, Adani Exports became top net foreign exchange earner in the country and the largest private sector Superstar Trading House in India', corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adani_Group ('By 1998, the firm became the top net foreign exchange earner for India Inc'). Under frame.md a dated qualitative industry-leading claim establishes that the crossing had already occurred; India's single largest net foreign-exchange earner in 1998 was necessarily orders of magnitude above that year's bar of $5,063,008 (about Rs 21 crore at the period's ~41 INR/USD). No currency conversion is load-bearing here because the margin is not close. Midpoint 1993. FLAGGED: the upper end of this bracket is a QUALITATIVE SCALE CLAIM doing the dating work, and its primary wording is the company's own -- acceptable for rev10 bounding (frame.md's 'company's own claim is not a ranking' rule governs rank1, not revenue), and independently repeated by Wikipedia, but it is the weakest link on this row. NARROWER BRACKET SOUGHT AND NOT FOUND: Adani Exports listed on the BSE and NSE on 1 November 1994 at Rs 150/share, 25x oversubscribed, and its 1990s turnover should exist in the prospectus and annual reports, but no published rupee revenue figure for any year between 1988 and 2000 was located after repeated attempts (Wikipedia on Gautam Adani, Adani Enterprises and Adani Group; adani.com and adanienterprises.com timelines); the 1994 listing year was rejected as an upper bound because a listing is not a revenue figure and using it would be the barred IPO fallback in disguise. a1: born 24 June 1962, Ahmedabad; CSV stores 1962. a2 UNKNOWN, and this is a genuine source conflict rather than a gap: Wikipedia states he 'was educated at Sheth Chimanlal Nagindas Vidyalaya school in Ahmedabad, but dropped out when he was 16', which leaves no COMPLETED credential to date, while the widely repeated alternative account has him finishing school and then dropping out of a Gujarat University B.Com in the second year. Neither version supplies a dated completed credential, so unknown is recorded rather than a guess, following p34 and p73. a3: 1978, diamond sorter for Mahendra Brothers in Mumbai -- his first paid work in the commodity trade that the hit entity is built on. a6: 2007, the Mundra Port and Special Economic Zone IPO, '116 times oversubscription' per Adani's own timeline.
